title: Holographic Properties of Compact Universes: A Unified Framework for 3-Torus and 3-Sphere Cosmologies
content: We present a unified cosmological model describing universes with finite compact topologies, specifically three-dimensional tori and three-spheres, within the framework of general relativity. The model employs a generalized FLRW metric with a discrete topological parameter characterizing the spatial geometry. We develop corresponding Friedmann equations using a hybrid formulation that explores modified dark energy dynamics, analyze background stability, and establish holographic characteristics of the Hubble radius. The mathematical framework is dimensionally consistent and provides a theoretical laboratory for studying the interplay between topology and holography in cosmology. A key feature is the natural emergence of a fundamental scale connecting local expansion dynamics to global topology through the cosmological constant. We identify and discuss an inherent tension between holographic principles and compact topologies in causally connected universes. While our modified formulation deviates from standard general relativity by a factor of two in the dark energy contribution, this theoretical exploration offers insights into how spatial topology influences cosmological evolution and challenges conventional applications of holography in finite spaces. The framework establishes a foundation for future investigations incorporating matter, radiation, and cosmological perturbations in compact geometries.
